edges.mechanism: Pyridoxine (B6) 10-25 mg accelerates peripheral aromatic amino acid decarboxylation of levodopa, reversing its effect; carbidopa blocks this, so relevant mainly to levodopa without a decarboxylase inhibitor.
Folic/folinic acid replenishes folate depleted by low-dose methotrexate, reducing GI and hepatic toxicity.
edges.evidence: Systematic review of 6 RCTs (n=624) in RA: GI AEs RR 0.74, transaminase elevation RR 0.23, MTX withdrawal RR 0.39; moderate GRADE.

edges.mechanism: Phenytoin lowers serum folate; folic acid supplementation in folate-deficient patients can lower phenytoin concentrations with possible seizure breakthrough.
edges.evidence: Narrative review of human studies and case reports; phenytoin label lists folic acid as decreasing phenytoin levels.

edges.mechanism: Metformin reduces vitamin B12 absorption; B complex B12 content may partly offset but B12 status should be monitored.
edges.evidence: Meta-analysis of 31 studies: B12 deficiency RR 2.09 (1.49-2.93), serum B12 MD -63.7 pmol/L, dose/duration dependent.

edges.mechanism: Gastric acid suppression may impair food-bound B12 absorption.
edges.evidence: Meta-analysis of 25 observational studies: OR 1.42 (1.16-1.73) for B12 deficiency, heterogeneous.

edges.mechanism: Folic acid can correct the megaloblastic anemia of B12 deficiency while neurologic damage progresses (masking), and may exacerbate B12 deficiency.
edges.evidence: Folic acid product label contraindication; 2024 review of mostly correlative/clinical-observation evidence.

edges.mechanism: High folic acid intake with low B12 status associated with worse cognition and higher homocysteine/MMA; B12 status should be assured when using folic-acid-containing complexes.
edges.evidence: Narrative review of correlative and uncontrolled clinical data.

edges.mechanism: High-dose vitamin B6 (pyridoxine) causes dose- and duration-dependent sensory axonal neuropathy; many B complexes contain 50-100 mg B6.
edges.evidence: EFSA 2023 UL 12 mg/day based on 50 mg/day reference point; systematic review of case data; Dutch pharmacovigilance shows cases even at lower doses.

edges.mechanism: Biotin in B complexes saturates streptavidin in biotin-streptavidin sandwich assays, giving falsely low TSH; competitive free T4/T3 assays read falsely high, mimicking hyperthyroidism/Graves disease.
edges.evidence: Reviews of assay design and FDA-reported cases; 2026 ETA guideline lists biotin as an interferent.

edges.mechanism: Biotin causes falsely low troponin in biotin-streptavidin assays, risking missed myocardial infarction.
edges.evidence: Spiking study: hs-cTnT negative bias 24% at 50 ug/L to 97-98% at 500-1000 ug/L biotin; reviews.

edges.mechanism: Biotin interference affects any biotin-streptavidin immunoassay, including reproductive hormones and immunosuppressive drug assays.
edges.evidence: Clinical chemistry best-practice review; 92 FDA reports since 2016.

edges.mechanism: Riboflavin is excreted in urine, producing bright yellow coloration; benign.
edges.evidence: RCT: oral riboflavin 400 mg significantly intensified urine yellow color.

edges.mechanism: Pharmacologic nicotinic acid (especially sustained-release) causes flushing and dose-related hepatotoxicity; adding stand-alone niacin to a B complex raises total dose.
High-dose nicotinic acid can cause aminotransferase elevations and acute liver injury.
In VITACOG, B-vitamin slowing of cognitive decline in MCI occurred only with higher baseline omega-3 (DHA) status.
edges.evidence: Post hoc analysis of one RCT (n=266).

edges.mechanism: Additional stand-alone biotin on top of a B complex increases serum biotin and immunoassay interference risk.
TT carriers show greater homocysteine at low folate and need higher serum folate (~15 ng/mL) to normalize homocysteine with folic acid.
edges.evidence: Post hoc analysis of CSPPT RCT (n=16,413).

edges.mechanism: Dialysis patients have high homocysteine; thiamine + folic acid improved cognition in one RCT.
